findings.claim: TidyFindings reports every '-' line in the go.mod part of the tidy diff that looks like a requirement. It does not check whether the same path is added back in a '+' line. When tidy only rewrites a still-required dependency, for example by adding or removing '// indirect' or by moving the entry between the direct and indirect blocks, the old line is reported as 'go.mod: require <path> <version>' although the requirement stays. This is the common outcome of removing an import of a module that another dependency still needs. It becomes a false T2 go-mod-tidy candidate on the head, and the head has no matching line at the base, so the sweep reports 'fired'. The doc comment says only 'removal-only' and the tests do not cover this case. The cost is a spurious candidate the sweeper must answer 'live', not a wrong delivery.
proof_refs: engine/review/sweep_test.go:561-585 (the test diff only pairs a removed '// indirect' line with an added line for a different module, golang.org/x/new, so the same-path rewrite is never exercised)

findings.claim: Tidy relies on 'go mod tidy -diff', which needs Go 1.23 or later, and on the module cache. On an older go the flag is rejected with a non-zero exit and no diff, so the sweep exits 2 and stores nothing. Unlike the missing-cache case, the usage text, README and CHANGELOG do not name the Go version requirement. Delivery is blocked with a message about a failed 'go mod tidy' and no hint about the version.
proof_refs: README.md and bin/lib/usage.sh changes (they mention only 'go on PATH' and the module cache)

evidence: Read the full diff at the scratchpad path.

Checked the Tidy failure rule: exit 0 means no finding, a non-zero exit with a diff is a run, and anything else means the tool did not run.
